svg.title: quick-titles — on-device session titles and descriptions for your coding agents
svg.desc: A Claude Code session in a terminal window on a black background. The tab strip reads "New session" and "pi agent". A prompt types itself into the composer at the bottom — the input row bounded above and below by two full-width rules — "refactor the auth middleware token expiry" — and is sent; it lands in the transcript above as a user turn prefixed with ">". A working line runs with the Claude Code asterisk spinner cycling through ✻ ✽ ✳ ✢ beside the gerund Thinking… and the hint "(esc to interrupt)". A "• UserPromptSubmit hook" line then appears with the command it runs, node user-prompt.mjs, and its output — hookSpecificOutput.sessionTitle. That sessionTitle is what types itself, character by character, into the tab in place of the struck-through "New session": "Auth middleware token expiry refactor". A separate row labelled quick-titles carries the description, which is quick-titles' own field and not a field the host emits. Footer: a status line carrying the working directory; and the ⏵⏵ accept-edits mode line.
